latest_release.name: MediaPipe v1.2.3
latest_release.body:
### Bazel changes

- Migrate `mediapipe::NoDestructor` to `absl::NoDestructor` (`absl/base/no_destructor.h`) in `mediapipe/framework` and remove obsolete `mediapipe/framework/deps/no_destructor.h`.
- Respect TensorBufferRequirements alignment in InferenceRunnerLiteRt
- Resolve file-path media parts in SemanticRetriever::Retrieve before embedding.
- [MediaPipe] Fix tensor view destruction deadlock on LiteRT run error.
- Register only the CPU accelerator in LiteRT environments for CPU-only runners.
- Add NPU dispatch library directory to C MpBaseOptions.
- Forward BaseOptions app telemetry in C++ tasks and Swift wrappers.
- Unify util/endian.h using absl/numeric/bits.h and remove deps/endian.h
- Format C++ code and fix includes in framework
- Format C++ code and fix includes in gpu
- Bump MediaPipe version to 1.2.3
- Support string input tensors in the MediaPipe LiteRT inference runner.
- Update Swift Package Manager files for the 1.2.3 iOS release.
- Added  C API classifier options conversion to MPPClassifierOptions+Helpers

### MediaPipe Tasks update
This section should highlight the changes that are done specifically for any platform and don't propagate to
other platforms.

#### Android
- Unify MediaPipe Tasks option, method, and result names across Python, Web, Android, and iOS while preserving deprecated compatibility aliases, and update DevSite guides and code snippets.

#### iOS
- Add pure Swift microphone audio recording for MediaPipe Tasks iOS.
- Add pure Swift vision running mode, image processing options, and segmentation mask for MediaPipe Tasks iOS.
- Add pure Swift vision image input container for MediaPipe Tasks iOS.
- Add C API image conversion and ScopedMpImage to MPPImage+Utils.
- Add C API task runner helpers and VisionCallbackPool to MPPVisionTaskRunner.
- Remove legacy iOS C++ task runners, packet creators, and protobuf helpers.
- Migrate TextClassifier to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate TextEmbedder to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate LanguageDetector to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate TextSummarizer to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate TextProofreader to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate AudioClassifier to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate UniversalEmbedder to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate ImageClassifier to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate ImageEmbedder to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate FaceDetector to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate ObjectDetector to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate FaceLandmarker to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate HandLandmarker to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate PoseLandmarker to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate HolisticLandmarker to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate GestureRecognizer to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate ImageSegmenter to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate InteractiveSegmenter to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Migrate InteractiveSegmenterLegacy to MediaPipe Tasks C API.
- Unify MediaPipe Tasks option, method, and result names across Python, Web, Android, and iOS while preserving deprecated compatibility aliases, and update DevSite guides and code snippets.

#### Javascript
- Remove on-disk cache options from the web audio LiteRT-LM tasks.
- Fix DecisionMaker Web SDK APIs, boolean scoring, and native in-memory CPU loading.
- Support incremental TextToSpeech stream input on the web.

#### Python
- Expose BooleanQuestion and ChoiceQuestion examples in the Decision Maker C API and Python.


### MediaPipe Dependencies
- Explicitly include direct headers and BUILD dependencies.
- Update MediaPipe Tasks Web WASM files.

detail.readme:
**Attention:** *See [https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/)
for the primary developer documentation site for MediaPipe.*

![MediaPipe](https://developers.google.com/static/mediapipe/images/home/hero_01_1920.png)

**On-device machine learning for everyone**

Delight your customers with innovative machine learning features. MediaPipe
contains everything that you need to customize and deploy to mobile (Android,
iOS), web, desktop, edge devices, and IoT, effortlessly.

*   [See demos](https://google-ai-edge.github.io/mediapipe-samples-web/#/home)
*   [Learn more](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions)

## Get started

You can get started with MediaPipe Solutions by following the developer guides
for each solution, including:

*   [audio](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/audio/audio_classifier)
*   [decision](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/decision/decision_maker)
*   [genai](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/genai/llm_inference)
*   [retrieval](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/retrieval/semantic_retriever)
*   [text](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/text/text_classifier)
*   [vision](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/object_detector)

If you need help setting up a development environment for use with MediaPipe
Tasks, follow our setup guides for:

*   [Android](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/setup_android)
*   [iOS](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/setup_ios)
*   [Python](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/setup_python)
*   [Web apps](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/setup_web)

## Solutions

MediaPipe Solutions provides a suite of libraries and tools for you to quickly
apply artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques in your
applications. You can plug these solutions into your applications immediately,
customize them to your needs, and use them across multiple development
platforms. MediaPipe Solutions is part of the MediaPipe [open source
project](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/mediapipe), so you can further
customize the solutions code to meet your application needs.

These libraries and resources provide the core functionality for each MediaPipe
Solution:

*   **MediaPipe Tasks**: Cross-platform APIs and libraries for deploying
    solutions. [Learn
    more](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/tasks).
*   **MediaPipe models**: Pre-trained, ready-to-run models for use with each
    solution.

To customize and evaluate solutions, use **MediaPipe Studio**. It lets you
visualize, test, and benchmark solutions in your browser.
[Learn more](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/studio) and
[see our demos](https://google-ai-edge.github.io/mediapipe-samples-web/).

## Framework

To start using MediaPipe Framework, [install MediaPipe
Framework](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/framework/getting_started/install)
and start building example applications in C++, Android, and iOS.

[MediaPipe Framework](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/framework) is
the low-level component used to build efficient on-device machine learning
pipelines, similar to the premade MediaPipe Solutions.

Before using MediaPipe Framework, familiarize yourself with the following key
[Framework
concepts](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/framework/framework_concepts/overview):

*   [Packets](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/framework/framework_concepts/packets)
*   [Graphs](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/framework/framework_concepts/graphs)
*   [Calculators](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/framework/framework_concepts/calculators)

## Community

*   [Discuss](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/mediapipe) - General
    community discussion around MediaPipe.
*   [Awesome MediaPipe](https://github.com/mgyong/awesome-mediapipe) - A
    curated list of awesome MediaPipe related frameworks, libraries and
    software.

## Contributing

We welcome contributions. Please follow these
[guidelines](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/mediapipe/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).

We use GitHub issues for tracking requests and bugs. Please post questions to
the MediaPipe Stack Overflow with a `mediapipe` tag.

## Privacy Notice

Last modified: June 5, 2026

When you use MediaPipe Tasks, processing of the input data (e.g. images, video,
text) takes place on device, and MediaPipe does not send that input data to
Google servers. As a result, you can use our MediaPipe Tasks APIs for processing
data that should not leave the device.

MediaPipe Tasks APIs send metrics about the performance and utilization of the
APIs in your app to Google. Google uses this metrics data to measure
performance, usage, debug, maintain and improve the MediaPipe Tasks, as further
described in our [Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy).

**You are responsible for obtaining informed consent from your app users about
Google's processing of MediaPipe metrics data as required by applicable law.**
